blind.description: A stylized wooden post-and-beam support structure or mine shoring frame consisting of two thick upright posts that flare slightly at the base, topped with a sturdy horizontal crossbeam. Small diagonal corner braces reinforce the inner angles, and rectangular collar bands with wedges secure the joints where the posts meet the lintel. Surfaces are solid, smooth, and hand-painted in dark brown weathered wood grain with subtle mossy undertones. It stands stably directly on the bases of its two posts.
blind.from_above: A single horizontal wooden beam running left to right, bordered by two raised rectangular collar fittings near either end, with a U-shaped post-and-lintel shadow cast diagonally onto the ground.
blind.height_vs_figure: About 7 feet tall (noticeably taller than the 5 ft 9 in figure) and about 5.5 to 6 feet wide across the top beam.
